lines: An additive oscillator that sums up to 128 sine partials, with controls for how many there are, how far apart they are spaced, how they are weighted and which of them are sieved out
Sets the pitch of the fundamental, 0 giving C0 at 16.35Hz and each whole step up an octave, over a range of seven octaves
Sets the spacing of the partials in units of the fundamental: at 1 the spectrum is harmonic, below 1 it is squeezed, above 1 stretched, and at 0 every partial lands on one frequency
Sets how many partials are summed, one at the far left and doubling with each step to 128 at the far right
Left of centre it tilts the weight of the spectrum towards the low partials; right of centre the weights go flat and the lowest partial climbs instead
Sieves partials out: turned up from the middle it removes the proper multiples of 2, then 3, then 5, leaving the primes; turned down it removes the primes from the top, leaving the octaves
Sets how long the amplitude CV takes to travel from one partial to the next, up to 8 seconds; fully clockwise it freezes the buffer, and with nothing in the amp jack it tunes a comb filter
Sets the depth of the linear through-zero frequency modulation from the fm jack, none at the far left
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, on the stretch CV
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, on the number of partials CV
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, on the tilt CV
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, on the sieve CV
Restarts every partial's phase together and draws fresh delays for the random buffer order
Sets the pitch of the fundamental at a volt per octave, added to the pitch knob; the number of channels here sets the polyphony of the whole module
Modulates the frequency linearly and through zero, scaled by the fm knob; it does not reach the root output
Adds to the stretch knob through its attenuverter, a volt covering a tenth of the knob's travel at full attenuation
Adds to the number of partials knob through its attenuverter, a volt covering a tenth of the knob's travel at full attenuation
Adds to the tilt knob through its attenuverter, a volt covering a tenth of the knob's travel at full attenuation
Adds to the sieve knob through its attenuverter, a volt covering a tenth of the knob's travel at full attenuation
The CV recorded into the eight-second buffer that sets the partial amplitudes, 10V meaning full; patching this switches the amplitude section on and the comb filter off
Adds to the amp delay knob, a volt covering a tenth of its travel
Steps the buffer on each reading above 2.5V, which turns the amp delay knob into a clock divider rather than a time
A reading above 2.5V restarts every partial's phase together, so this can be used for oscillator sync
The summed partials for the left channel, up to 5V either way
The summed partials for the right channel, up to 5V either way; with nothing patched here both sums carry the same signal
The fundamental on its own as a sine wave, raised an octave for each octave the lowest partial has climbed; no frequency modulation reaches it
Note — the amplitude section does nothing until a cable is in the amp jack; with none there the amp delay knob tunes a comb filter instead
Note — the number of partials, the tilt, the sieve and the whole amplitude section are worked out once every 64 samples, so they cannot be modulated at audio rate; pitch, fm and stretch can
Note — the module resets and falls silent while all three of its outputs are unpatched
Note — the spectrogram along the top runs left to right from 0Hz to half the sample rate, with amplitude on a logarithmic scale; the left channel is drawn yellow and the right red
Menu — Quantize pitch knob: Continuous, Semitones, Octaves — snaps the pitch knob only, leaving the V/oct input unquantised
Menu — Quantize stretch: Continuous, Consonants, Harmonics — snaps the stretch after the knob and its CV are added; Consonants snaps to pure intervals, Harmonics to whole numbers
Menu — Stereo mode: Mono, Soft-panned, Hard-panned — spreads the partials across the two sum outputs, and it only takes effect while the right output is patched
Menu — CV buffer order: Low→high, High→low, Random — sets the order the amplitude CV travels through the partials
Menu — Empty buffer on reset — clears the amplitude buffer on a reset instead of leaving what is already in it

Ad.notes: The fundamental frequency is the pitch knob plus the V/oct jack as an exponent of two times 16.35159783128741466737, the literal at Ad.cpp:270, which is C0. The knob runs -1 to 6, so seven octaves; the maker's manual says nine, which is the reach of the spectrum rather than of the knob. The CV scalings are at lines 177-184 and 257-258 and are all fractions of the knob travel, not volts per unit. The reset and clock jacks are plain level tests against 2.5V (lines 158 and 227), not Schmitt triggers, so a slow signal can retrigger them. The stereo mode in the menu is overridden to Mono whenever the right sum output is unpatched (lines 247-250). The panel prints 'root' over the third output while the maker's tooltip calls it 'fundamental'.

Adje.notes: Adje reads every input with getVoltage() rather than getPolyVoltage, which the maker's manual states plainly: the CV inputs are monophonic and the polyphony is only on the outputs, where the channel count comes from the Channels menu item rather than from any jack. The octave knob is rounded unconditionally at Adje.cpp:141, so unlike Ad's pitch knob there is no continuous option for it. The number-of-partials CV is scaled 1.4 per volt against Ad's 0.7, and pushing the total below zero flips the sign of the stretch (line 191), which has no equivalent on Ad.

Bufke.notes: The reset input and the reset button carry no configInput or configParam name, so hovering either shows nothing; the panel prints 'reset' beside them. Bufke pushes the raw voltage into its buffer (Bufke.cpp:173) where Ad scales by a tenth first, so the output carries the same voltages that went in. With no parent the module falls back to sixteen channels and partial numbers 1 to 16 (lines 111-114). The buffer is four seconds long, matching Adje rather than Ad's eight.

Funs.notes: The two outputs are the two roots of the same phase-distortion equation, which is why the module has two of them rather than a mix control; the maker's manual works the algebra through. XMAX_PARAM is declared in the ParamId enum but never configured and never given a widget, so it cannot be reached at all.

Sjoegele.notes: The length knob is -6 to 0 and is raised as a power of ten to give metres (Sjoegele.cpp:63-68), so the panel's 1µm, 1mm and 1m marks are the ends and the middle of its travel. Gravity is 9.8 times two to the power of the knob, -6 to 6, so the centre is Earth. Friction is ten to the power of eight times the knob, minus one. The two angle outputs are 5V when high, not 10V (lines 111-112), although the maker's manual only says 'high gate'. The panel order of the six outputs is not their index order: the two angle outputs are indexes 4 and 5 and sit at the right of the two rows, after x and y.

Sjang.notes: The two randomness knobs are mapped exponentially at Sjang.cpp:107-108, (100 to the power of the knob, minus one, over 99), so the bottom of their travel is very fine. The second output uses oscillators 16 to 31 (line 118 and line 140) and is skipped entirely while it is unpatched, which saves processor time; the maker names the two outputs left and right in configOutput while the panel prints 'wave 1' and 'wave 2'. The right-hand destruct knob is DESTRUCT_A_PARAM, named 'destruct amp' in the tooltip, while the panel prints 'destruct shape' and the matching input is named 'destruct shape'. The reset and randomize buttons are added to their jacks before the Schmitt trigger, so pressing a button and patching its jack both work through the same detector.
